CSP Co Siderurgica do Pecem Appoints New Chief Financial Officer Amid Expansion Efforts

CSP Co Siderurgica do Pecem, a leading Brazilian steel manufacturer, announced the appointment of Renata Albuquerque as its new Chief Financial Officer (CFO) on Thursday, effective immediately. The move comes as the company pursues a series of strategic initiatives to expand its production capacity and strengthen its financial footing in a competitive global steel market.

Albuquerque brings more than 20 years of experience in corporate finance and risk management, having previously held senior roles at several major industrial firms in Brazil. In her new position, she will oversee CSP’s financial strategy, investor relations, and capital allocation as the company seeks to capitalize on growing demand for high-grade steel, particularly in the construction and infrastructure sectors.

“We are pleased to welcome Renata to our executive team,” said CEO Luis Cordeiro in a statement. “Her deep understanding of industrial operations and disciplined approach to financial management will be critical as we embark on the next phase of our growth journey.”

CSP Co Siderurgica do Pecem operates one of the largest integrated steel plants in northeastern Brazil, with annual production capacity exceeding 3 million metric tons. The company recently unveiled plans to invest approximately R$1.2 billion over the next three years to upgrade its blast furnaces and expand its product portfolio, focusing on value-added flat steel products.

According to industry analysts, the appointment signals a commitment to robust financial governance as CSP navigates fluctuating raw material costs and evolving customer requirements. “This is a prudent move for CSP,” said Marcos Ferraz, metals sector analyst at the Brazilian Association for Industrial Development. “Strong financial leadership will be essential as the company steps up its expansion and faces both domestic and international competition.”

Union representatives have also welcomed the appointment. “We look forward to working with Ms. Albuquerque to ensure stable employment and the continued growth of the plant,” said José Oliveira, president of the local steelworkers’ union.

CSP’s board expressed confidence that Albuquerque’s expertise will provide a “steady hand” during the implementation of its capital projects and reinforce the company’s commitment to sustainable growth.

Albuquerque stated, “I am honored to join CSP at this important moment and look forward to helping drive value for our shareholders, employees, and the wider community.”
